findings.claim: 0.3: 'None of the 189 v8 descriptor members changed on main ... So the v8 digest 7b22c1f4... survives A1's rebase'. 2.4: 'The v8 digest is final.' 7.2 C09: 'recomputes v8 7b22c1f4..., v7 0055de6c... and v5 fca86d74... unchanged'.
findings.verified_evidence: Refuted. The members did not change on main, but two members are derived from the base commit and will be rebuilt. (1) owner-sources.json and source-citations.json are v8 members: Plans/workflow_combined_source_contracts/installed-profile.json:613 and :743 @origin/plans/replan-v8-a1-20260925 (A1). (2) owner-sources.json @A1 rows carry "base_commit": "63cf2cb97f936c91..." and whole_sha256_at_base; I recomputed at origin/main bd95afcc8: Contracts_V0.md, Decision_Log.md and storage-plan.md no longer match their pins. (3) source-citations.json @A1 landing_base.commit is 63cf2cb97 with rule 'the compile rebase re-derives the registry rows, the descriptors and these citations at the landing base'. (4) reports/event-authority-20260911/replan-v8/STATUS.md:80 @A1: 'If it reports any other change, follow root condition 1 in full: rebuild, re-run run_all.py, re-freeze ... update the digests in CV-354 and ATS-059'; Plans/storage_value_registry.json changed on main since 63cf2cb97 (git diff --name-only 63cf2cb97 origin/main), so the merged-registry hash cannot reproduce. (5) Package scripts (read-only checkout /home/user/pmpkg-push, replan-v8/goal-replan-v8-canonical-draft-20260925/v1): scripts/author.py:999 writes ("base_commit", ctx.a.base); scripts/rebase_check.py:72 runs the build with "--base", lb. (6) Corroboration, not canon: that checkout is on branch replan-v8-canonical-draft-20260925-rebase1 (commit 344fd08 'move BASE to the landing base bd95afcc8c'); its uncommitted working-tree after/Plans/workflow_combined_source_contracts/installed-profile-digest.txt (15:33Z) reads 0da022d2..., while the committed file reads 7b22c1f4.... C09 as written would fail against A1 as it will land.
findings.suggested_repair: Drop 'final' and 'survives'. Take the v8 digest only from A1 as landed. Have profile-branches.json, C09 and C12 read it from the landed descriptor, and write every 7b22c1f4... mention as 'the v8 digest at A1's landing (7b22c1f4... at e8d61ace4)'. Re-cite every A1 line number after A1's canon recompile (the rebase rewrites CV-354 and ATS-059 at least).

findings.claim: The Replan consumer is 'Not adopted in A2' and the release projection admission is 'Not supplied. Stated in GRS-090 with the reason'.
findings.verified_evidence: The reason is sound: Plans/workflow_combined_source_contracts/replan/schemas/workflow-replan-source.v1.schema.json:212-213 @A1 fixes original_projection to '...goal_run_started_cancelled_replanned_consumer.v1.schema.json#/$defs/ReplanProjectResult' (checked). But canon assigns this to A2 in many places, and the design leaves them saying so after A2 lands: Plans/Goal_Runtime_System.md:8104-8105 @A1 'Replan release is unavailable until the consumer-adoption work A2 supplies the projection admission'; :8141 @A1 'Replan release and projection stay unavailable until A2'; Plans/Executor_Protocol.md:8887-8888 @A1 'release stays unavailable until A2 and A3 supply its projection admission'; Plans/Contracts_V0.md:23557-23559 @A1 'its adoption ... is separate required work (the consumer-adoption work A2)'; external-consumer-adoption-boundary.json:14 @A1. The program plan also gives it to A2: reports/event-authority-20260911/step-08-remaining-source-work-plan-20260924.md:118 @origin/main (A2 edits 'a new replanned consumer; a GRS-085 successor; projection families') and :119 (A3: 'replanned needs A1 and A2'). The design only routes ATS-059 (4.3) and freezes the descriptor 'consumer' literal (1.4). T-11 covers chain order, not this transfer.
findings.suggested_repair: Add dated routing notes (outside the unit YAML, as Goal_Runtime_System.md:2657 @origin/main) after GRS-087, EP-126, SP-321, CV-354, ATS-060 and BRS-031, and in the A1 index section, saying A2 landed without the Replan projection admission and naming where it now sits (C-A2-1). Add a process item: the step-08 plan rows 118-119 change, so the coordinator and A3 must accept that A3-replanned (or v9) owns the Replan consumer. Keep boundary :14 listed as open in GRS-090.

findings.claim: Cancelled v8 is 'authored, dormant' so 'a later D06 binding' does not force a new successor; certified v8 is 'authored, unavailable', and when admissions land 'A fresh generation is staged'.
findings.verified_evidence: The design never says how a dormant or unavailable branch becomes live without a byte change. Its own rule (0.2, anchor recipe 2.6 with profile_digest) makes any v6 byte change move the anchor. 6.3 pins the six goal_run rows by fingerprint but does not say whether that pin sits in a digest member; a later certified row revision (C-A2-2 or v9) changes fingerprint f58cc6a7 (recomputed @origin/main). 9.2's v7 row adds only 'v9 started, cancelled, certified' plus stopped, so no chain member is named to make v8 certified live. The A3-stopped design section 5 table expects v6 'certified for v7, and for v8 once A2 adopts it'.
findings.suggested_repair: State in GRS-090 and protocol P-sections that each gate is a runtime source-admission condition written in v6's bytes. List which pins sit in digest members and which do not. Name the chain member that makes v8 certified live, or say v8 certified is never projected and tell A3.

findings.claim: 'v6's pin files sit outside its digest (3.4), so a reseal never forces a copy or moves v6's anchor.'
findings.verified_evidence: resource-realms.json is a digest member (3.1 table: 'yes'). v5's Plans/goal_run_certified_consumer_contracts/resource-realms.json @origin/main pins 1006 whole-file SHA-256 values (my count; 0 stale today).
